summary: A white light on a ledge-bound point at Muscongus Bay, Maine: an 1827 light, a second tower, keepers to 1934 and a museum house today.

corrections.why: The 1827 tower was replaced; the present tower dates from 1835 per USLHS and ALF. The 1985 nomination's 1857 rebuild and 34 ft square tower are in conflict and are noted in the story.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1827 date belongs to the first tower. ALF and USLHS date the surviving conical tower to 1835. The 1985 nomination's 'rebuilt in 1857' is not matched by any other source we read; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Conflicts left open in the story: (1) first tower/rebuild dates: NRHP 1827 built, rebuilt 1857, square 34 ft tower vs USLHS and ALF conical tower 1835, 38 ft; (2) lens 1856 (USLHS, ALF) vs 1857 (LighthouseFriends); (3) fog bell removal 1930 (ALF) vs 1937 (LighthouseFriends); (4) keeper's house to the State 1934 (NRHP) vs Bristol purchase 1940 (LighthouseFriends). Roster lines were matched by position and name in the USLHS record (the place record is the roster source; the roster is also on LighthouseFriends). The Life-Saving Service table entry is a list line only. Newspaper search (Chronicling America, Maine) found nothing useful for the Marr retirement; LighthouseFriends quotes the Kennebec Journal, footnoted to LighthouseFriends. No woman who kept the light appears in any source read. The current tower's lens status is not verified beyond the record. Hours from LighthouseFriends are not current; check the ALF page before publication. Pointe aux Barques, Franklin Island and Two Lights are other stations; only Two Lights is cited, via LighthouseFriends. The 1891 and 1892 Lighthouse Board entries are the Pemaquid lines 44 and 45 (scan pages 51 and 377). Fact-check pass 2026-10-22: the Lewis inspection of 1842 is called a lighthouse inspector, not a Lighthouse Board inspector (the Board dates from 1852). The Bulletin items were confirmed on their pages (1927 PDF p. 53, in the December 1927 issue; 1930 PDF p. 43, in the November 1930 issue). The 1888 table is Table 66, a list of places where vessels stranded during the last ten years. The LighthouseFriends quotations (Lewis 1842, Dunham's certificate of 1835, Mariner's logbook of 1873) are public-domain originals as LighthouseFriends prints them; the story footnotes LighthouseFriends for each. The NRHP nomination's 1934 transfer and state-park description conflict with the Bristol purchase of 1940 and the 1985 owner listing; the story states both.
